# `silk/core/hint`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Facts and branch weights that guide the optimizer without changing what a program computes.

## When to use
Use these functions in measured hot code: a state machine whose rare branches slow its common
path, or a check the optimizer cannot prove redundant. Ordinary code needs none of them.

## Details
[`likely`](#likely) and [`unlikely`](#unlikely) return their condition unchanged and only weigh the branch that tests
it, as C's `__builtin_expect` does. [`assume`](#assume) and [`unreachable`](#unreachable) are unsafe: they state a fact
the caller proves, the optimizer removes checks and paths that contradict it, and a false fact is
undefined behavior. Static evaluation runs `likely` and `unlikely` as their condition.

## Examples
### Weigh a rare branch and drop a check the caller proved
```silk
import silk.core.hint
import silk.num.u32

fn scaled(value: u32, shift: u32) -> u32 {
  if hint.unlikely(value == 0) {
    return 1
  }
  // The callers pass a shift below 32, so the shift needs no range check.
  unsafe { hint.assume(shift < 32) }
  return u32.shiftLeft(value, shift)
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  if scaled(3, 2) != 12 || scaled(0, 5) != 1 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `hint` with `import silk.core.hint as hint`.

## `likely`

```silk
pub fn likely(condition: bool) -> bool
```

Returns `condition` and weighs the branch that tests it as usually taken.

### Details

The result is always `condition`. The optimizer lays out the true path as the fall-through
path and moves the false path out of the way.

<a id="unlikely"></a>

## `unlikely`

```silk
pub fn unlikely(condition: bool) -> bool
```

Returns `condition` and weighs the branch that tests it as rarely taken.

### Details

The result is always `condition`. The optimizer lays out the false path as the fall-through
path and moves the true path out of the way.

<a id="assume"></a>

## `assume`

```silk
pub unsafe fn assume(condition: bool) -> ()
```

States that `condition` holds, so the optimizer can remove checks that it makes redundant.

### Details

In an optimized build the call emits no code. Later checks that `condition` decides, such as a
bounds check or a shift count test, fold away.

### Gotchas

The caller must prove `condition`. When it is false, the behavior is undefined, and a build may
skip a check that would have trapped.

<a id="unreachable"></a>

## `unreachable`

```silk
pub unsafe fn unreachable() -> never
```

Marks a point that execution never reaches.

### Details

The optimizer treats every path that leads here as dead and removes it, along with the tests
that select it.

### Gotchas

The caller must prove that no execution reaches the call. Reaching it is undefined behavior,
not a trap. Use `Intrinsic.trap` for a point that stops the program when reached.
